reason: The counted arithmetic event has a random logarithmic width determined by the same integer that is being factorized. Its proof is not an independent-radius estimate or an immediate consequence of a Dirichlet limit. It must isolate a square-full part with a usable moment, remove the arbitrary prime-power allocation law through its unit total mass, reduce the coprime square-free part to alpha^(omega(d))*(1−alpha)^(omega(m)), and choose complementary hyperbola ranges to keep the bound uniform near both logarithmic boundary faces. This coordinated reduction is beyond a routine qualifying-exam application of a mean-value estimate and supports H2. The familiar mean-value input and final summation are not counted as new difficulty.
core_assessment:
square_full_moment: 517–537: n=a*b with b the largest square-full divisor and a=n-flat; the sum overa usesalpha<1 and the square-full sum converges forbeta<1/2. Applying this atalpha=beta=1/3 gives1375 and an O(1/logx) exceptional probability. That error is bounded by the targetDelta because its two denominator exponents sum to1.
dependent_width_dyadization: 1379–1399 sorts the same integer byn-flat in(x/z,2x/z], so the event itself supplies the multiplicative window for d_i. No independence of d_i andn-flat or of their widths is assumed. The notation log_2x meansloglogx, not a base2 logarithm; the chosen dyadic range remains withinz<=log^4x for large x.
arbitrary_allocation_law: 1402–1413: s(n) andn-flat are coprime. Hence the permitted multiplicativity factors the allocation weights, and summing all square-full allocations gives1. On the square-free component the weight is exactly the prime-color product; summing the other colors yields(1−alpha)^(omega(m)). This is why the bound is uniform over the allowedf andk.
hyperbola_and_endpoints: 1414–1445 drops square-free/coprimality restrictions only to enlarge a nonnegative sum, counts square-full b<=z byO(sqrt z), and dividesdm<=2x/z into d-small or m-small. The d-small region forcesu<=2/3 and the m-small region forcesu>=1/3 oncex is large. Consequently the mean-value/harmonic-window estimates yield the correct complementary endpoint factors rather than a bound that degenerates asu→0 or1.
harmonic_window_and_final_sum: 1678–1700 proves the required short harmonic-window consequence from the allowed mean value estimate, Euler products and partial summation. If a window centerx^u is below2, its harmless enlargement to2 fits the stated input range and the1+u*logx factor. The remaining dyadic sum oflog z/sqrt z is convergent, completing the probability estimate uniformly.
prerequisite_assessment: The specified mean-value bound foralpha^omega, ordinary Mertens/partial summation andO(sqrt z) counting of square-full integers are sufficient. Neither the boundary probability nor a distributional independence statement is supplied. The square-full moment argument and the proof-specific two-range factorization remain local obligations. Small boundedx is harmless since the right side is bounded below by an absolute positive constant and the probability is at most1.

standard_prerequisites.name: Counting square-full integers
standard_prerequisites.statement: There are O(sqrt z) square-full integers at most z; each can be written a^2b^3 with b square-free, and sum_b b^(-3/2) converges.
standard_prerequisites.use: Bound the square-full allocation count and the moment sum. No boundary probability estimate is supplied.

core_obligations: Use multiplicativity to remove arbitrary allocations of the square-full part while retaining a controlled window for the square-free divisor.
Translate the k-coordinate allocation weights exactly to alpha^omega(d)*(1-alpha)^omega(m) on the square-free part.
Track the dyadic square-free scale and split the factor pair at sqrt(2x/z), maintaining uniform control near u=0 and u=1.
Sum the scale loss(log z)/sqrt z after excluding the small square-free part using a fractional moment.

proof_roadmap.step: A square-full divisor moment makes N-flat<=x/(log x)^3 negligible; then decompose the remaining event by dyadic x/N-flat.
Separate square-free and square-full prime powers, sum out the latter allocations, and reduce to a weighted divisor pair with product of order x/z.
Use two asymmetric hyperbola regions and the weighted mean/harmonic bounds to recover both endpoint factors uniformly.
Provide the author Euler-product/partial-summation proof for the harmonic-window tool rather than assuming that local estimate for free.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: The input mean-value bound does not locate the factorization near x^u or control the random square-free deficit. The proof must decouple arbitrary multiplicative allocation weights on the square-full part, identify the exact two complementary square-free weights, and choose a dyadic/hyperbola split that retains the distinct u and1-u endpoint exponents uniformly in alpha and the allocation rule f. This is a nonroutine analytic-number-theoretic probability estimate, proposed as H2 for independent review.
